accounts.title: Connected accounts
accounts.subtitle: Facebook pages and groups this workspace can publish to.
accounts.noneBody: Connect the Facebook account that manages your pages. We ask for permission to list your pages and publish posts on their behalf, and store the resulting tokens encrypted.
accounts.reconnectPrompt: Reconnect this account to resume scheduled posts.
accounts.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect {name}? Scheduled posts to its pages and groups will be cancelled. Published history is kept.
accounts.groupsDisabled: Group publishing is turned off. Meta restricted the Groups API in April 2024, so it needs a separately approved permission and the app must be installed in each group.

ads.none: No ad account is connected. Finding them needs the ads read permission.
ads.hint: Spend next to organic reach, so a jump in reach can be told apart from a jump in budget.
ads.actionsHint: Every action type the campaigns produced, summed over the range.
ads.noCampaigns: No campaign data in this range.
ads.reachNote: Campaign reach shows the highest single day rather than a sum, because reach counts people and adding daily figures would count the same person twice.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.subtitle: Everything the Facebook Graph API will give us for this page
analytics.noPages: No Facebook pages are connected yet.
analytics.syncFailed: Could not read analytics from Facebook.
analytics.noData: Nothing captured yet. Pull from Facebook to fill this in.
analytics.unavailableTitle: {count, plural, one {# metric Facebook did not return} other {# metrics Facebook did not return}}
analytics.unavailableHint: Meta removes insights metrics between API versions. These were requested and refused, so they are listed rather than silently dropped.
analytics.footnote: Figures come from the Facebook Graph API for {name}. Snapshots are stored here because Graph serves only about two years of history.
analytics.byPostHint: One row per post per destination — the same post can perform very differently on two pages, and averaging that away hides the signal.
analytics.noPosts: No published posts in this range.
analytics.reactionsByTypeHint: Like, love, wow, haha, sorry and anger.
analytics.noBreakdown: Facebook returned no breakdown for this range.
analytics.audienceHint: Demographics are lifetime snapshots from Facebook, so they show the audience as it stands now. New and lost likes are counted over the selected range.
analytics.coverageHint: The catalogue is every metric Meta documents. This is how much of it this destination has actually been shown to serve — untested means never asked for, which is not the same as refused.
analytics.coverageKey: Darker is served by Facebook; lighter was asked for and refused. The remainder has not been tested yet.

setup.title: Set up MS Social Pilot
setup.subtitle: Four things stand between this server and a scheduled post. This page keeps track of them.

setup.saveFailed: That could not be saved. Check the values and try again.

account.title: Create the owner account
account.body: The first account owns this installation and can invite everybody else. Registration closes to strangers as soon as it exists.
account.done: An account exists, and new colleagues now arrive by invitation.

facebookApp.title: Add your Facebook app
facebookApp.body: Publishing goes through a Meta app that you own. Create one at developers.facebook.com, then paste its ID and secret here.
facebookApp.hint: While the app is in Development mode, everything works for people who hold a role on it — Admin, Developer or Tester — with no review from Meta. Add your colleagues there and you can skip app review entirely.

connect.title: Connect a Facebook account
connect.body: Sign in with Facebook so this app can see the Pages and Groups you manage.

destination.title: Turn on a Page or Group
destination.body: Choose which of your Pages and Groups this workspace may publish to. Nothing goes out until at least one is on.
destination.done: At least one destination is ready to publish.

email.title: Set up email
email.body: Without it, a failed post fails silently: nobody is told, and it is found when a client asks why their page went quiet.
email.done: Email is configured, so failures reach somebody.
